generationContext.text:
# Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB is a fully managed NoSQL database for modern app development. Single-digit millisecond response times, and automatic and instant scalability, guarantee speed at any scale.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Automation resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.CosmosDB
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.subtype: Keyspace add-tag workflow with unsupported update fallback
proposals.explanation: The sync/async AddTag methods validate key/value. When CanUseTagResource returns true they fetch and modify tag-resource data, submit it with WaitUntil.Completed and refresh the keyspace through the REST client/pipeline into a typed resource response. Otherwise they fetch current data and modify Tags, but the cited internal Update methods immediately throw NotSupportedException rather than performing the fallback PUT.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated Custom partial implements both complete public tag-workflow bodies and explicit throwing fallback methods, rather than merely declaring generated operations.

proposals.subtype: Keyspace replace-tags workflow with unsupported update fallback
proposals.explanation: SetTags/SetTagsAsync validate the dictionary and, in the tag-resource branch, delete existing tags, fetch tag-resource data, replace its values, submit the new data and refresh the keyspace via the REST pipeline. The other branch replaces current resource-data Tags then calls the shown internal Update overload, which throws instead of issuing a fallback update.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete sync/async tag replacement and throwing fallback code are supplied by a Custom partial outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Keyspace remove-tag workflow with unsupported update fallback
proposals.explanation: RemoveTag/RemoveTagAsync validate the key, remove it from fetched tag-resource data, submit that data and refresh the typed keyspace response when the tag-resource branch is selected. Otherwise they remove the key from fetched resource-data Tags before the shown Update overload throws NotSupportedException.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial outside Generated contains executable public remove-tag methods and their explicit unsupported fallback implementation.

proposals.subtype: Throughput add-tag workflow adapting data into PUT content
proposals.explanation: AddTag/AddTagAsync validate inputs and either mutate/submit tag-resource data followed by a typed throughput-resource refresh, or fetch current throughput data, modify Tags and call local Update. That fallback constructs ThroughputSettingsUpdateData from Location and Properties?.Resource, copies tags and delegates to CreateOrUpdate with the supplied wait/cancellation arguments.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Custom partial implements complete public tag workflows and the data-to-PUT fallback adapter outside Generated; the nonempty implementations, not dependencies alone, establish customization.

proposals.subtype: Throughput replace-tags workflow adapting data into PUT content

The local fallback copies the resulting tags, Location and nested Resource into ThroughputSettingsUpdateData and forwards to CreateOrUpdate rather than passing resource data directly.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Explicit sync/async replacement workflows and the shared concrete request-model conversion are implemented in Custom outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Throughput remove-tag workflow adapting data into PUT content
proposals.explanation: RemoveTag/RemoveTagAsync validate the key and either remove it from tag-resource data, submit and refresh the typed throughput resource, or remove it from fetched throughput-data Tags. proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated Custom partial contains complete remove-tag workflow bodies plus an explicit shared data-to-update-content adapter.

The other branch fetches table data and changes its Tags, then invokes the cited internal Update overload that immediately throws rather than sending PUT content.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete public tag-operation bodies and explicit throwing update fallbacks are handwritten in the Custom partial outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Table replace-tags workflow with unsupported update fallback

proposals.subtype: Table remove-tag workflow with unsupported update fallback
